Title: Retained Runtime Execution Evidence
Notes: Runtime attempts retain factual evidence; compact evidence summary provided for failed/blocked executions. Diagnostics bundle (diagnostics/diagnostics-manifest.json + per-attempt subdirs) retains environment fingerprint, pre-launch baseline, and failure classification for cold-start root-cause analysis. Windows host-native compare hardens LabVIEWCLI.ini connect-window keys (OpenAppReferenceTimeoutInSecond and AfterLaunchOpenAppReferenceTimeoutInSecond) before each run via configurable `viHistorySuite.runtime.cliConnectTimeoutSeconds`; the doctor summary surfaces the hardening applied/requestedValue line on `labview-cli-connection-failed` failures so operators can confirm the fix from packet output without opening the diagnostics manifest. The Windows-container LabVIEW CLI script builder accepts the same `cliConnectTimeoutSeconds` value so container and host-native runs harden the connect window identically. The Linux container LabVIEW CLI script builder reaches the same parity: before launch it widens the connect window in the per-version LabVIEW `.conf` the launched headless LabVIEW reads (OpenAppReferenceTimeoutInSecond and AfterLaunchOpenAppReferenceTimeoutInSecond, default 180s, configurable via the same `viHistorySuite.runtime.cliConnectTimeoutSeconds`) and runs the CLI exactly once (single-cycle timed loop, no in-script -350000 retry), so the connect-window hardening addresses a slow cold LabVIEW launch and any residual VI Server connectivity failure surfaces as a genuine nonzero exit; all `.conf` mutation is fail-soft.

Title: Linux Host-Native Headless Comparison Invocation
Notes: Linux host-native LabVIEWCLI invocations are always headless (they unconditionally pass -Headless, matching the Docker Linux image, with no opt-out env var); the Linux container provider likewise invokes LabVIEWCLI with -Headless. Stderr classification adds labview-cli-create-report-permission-error and recognizes Failed to initialize headless LabVIEW. as linux-headless-init-failed; either Linux headless reason wins over generic stderr/diagnostic-log reasons. The comparison runs a single attempt (single-cycle timed loop) with no headless-session-reset retry, so a classified headless failure is surfaced as a genuine result. Before launch, Linux host-native labview-cli runs read labview.conf (under ~/natinst/.config/LabVIEW-<version>/, ~/.config/natinst/LabVIEW-<version>/, or /etc/natinst/LabVIEW-<version>/) and block execution with linux-vi-server-tcp-disabled when server.tcp.enabled=False, when the key is absent, or when no candidate config is readable (NI Linux defaults VI Server TCP off); when requestedLabviewVersion is unset the year is inferred from the resolved labviewExe directory (e.g. LabVIEW-2026-64). The lvcompare engine is exempt from this preflight. When TCP is enabled the resolved server.tcp.port (default 3363) is passed to LabVIEWCLI as -PortNumber. Linux host-native staging mirrors VI inputs and report output under a short tmpdir (default $TMPDIR/vi-history-suite-runtime, overridable via LVIE_LINUX_RUNTIME_TMPDIR, opt-out via LVIE_LINUX_DISABLE_RUNTIME_TMPDIR=1) using a directory-boundary check so similarly-prefixed paths do not bypass the workaround for LabVIEW 2026 Linux path-table corruption.

The doctor also runs an advisory system-clock-skew preflight (injectable now + authoritative-time collaborators; advisory unknown when the source is unreachable; --fail-on-clock-skew opts into a hard failure) that surfaces the dual-boot clock-skew trap which silently knocks the runner offline with a misleading GitHub registration-deleted error.

Title: Concurrent LabVIEW Version Conflict Diagnostic
Notes: Compare-time peer of the open-time VHS-REQ-637 version gate and sibling of the compare-time VHS-REQ-621 bitness block. comparisonRuntimeLocator.locate short-circuits to blockedReason=windows-host-version-conflict when a running LabVIEW.exe has a known year differing from the requested viHistorySuite.labviewVersion while the bitness matches; the year is inferred best-effort via inferLabviewYearFromExecutablePath and an unknown running year never blocks. The selection retains hostObservedLabviewVersion; comparisonRuntimeDoctor names the observed and selected years and offers a Docker-backed x64 recovery; the pre-launch windows-host-version-conflict block now surfaces a concise close plus Retry Compare toast and suppresses the auto-opened report while still persisting the packet mirroring VHS-REQ-621 (#530). Host-native LabVIEW CLI only. The shared VHS-REQ-622 Windows runtime-conflict harness adds version-A (host 2025/selected 2026) and version-B (host 2026/selected 2025) real-hardware scenarios asserting windows-host-version-conflict on the dispatch-only self-hosted maintainer runner.

Title: LabVIEW VI Version Too New Compare Failure Diagnostic
Notes: Compare-time peer of the running-session conflict diagnostics VHS-REQ-621 and VHS-REQ-653: fires when the running and selected LabVIEW agree but the VI file was saved in a newer LabVIEW than the selected engine. classifyRuntimeFailure reclassifies a nonzero exit whose stderr carries the LabVIEW 0x465 File version is later than the current LabVIEW version signature to labview-vi-version-too-new ahead of the generic command-exited-nonzero fallback. isViVersionTooNewFailure plus buildViVersionTooNewMessage drive a concise Pick Runtime Provider toast that names the selected LabVIEW and steers to pick a newer installed LabVIEW while the verbose runtime-failure message is suppressed; the action returns the dedicated failed-vi-version-too-new outcome and does not auto-open the report webview (the toast is the only surface) while still persisting the packet mirroring the #530 host-conflict gates (#597). comparisonRuntimeDoctor emits a matching forward-version next-action. Host-native compare-time only (#595).

Title: Reactive Runtime Provider Selection And Quick-Pick

When the selected docker image platform conflicts with the confirmed active Docker daemon mode the label renders a warning state with a conflict tooltip; the mode must be confirmed (explicit override or successful docker info probe) so an unknown mode never warns against a host-OS guess.

Title: Concurrent LabVIEW Bitness Conflict Diagnostic
Notes: Windows host preflight infers running LabVIEW bitness from Get-Process executable path (Program Files vs Program Files (x86)) and propagates labviewProcessBitness/labviewProcessExecutablePath through RuntimeProcessObservation. comparisonRuntimeLocator.locate short-circuits to blockedReason=windows-host-bitness-conflict when observed bitness differs from selected; comparisonRuntimeDoctor emits a next-action naming both bitnesses and viHistorySuite.labviewBitness. classifyRuntimeFailure rewrites command-exited-nonzero to labview-host-bitness-conflict when exit-snapshot LabVIEW bitness mismatches. Title: LabVIEW CLI Prerequisite Gate For VI History Open

Title: LabVIEW CLI Install Offer When LabVIEW Is Installed

Title: Windows Host-Native VI Server TCP Preflight Parity
Notes: Before launching LabVIEWCLI, Windows host-native labview-cli runs read the LabVIEW.ini adjacent to the selected LabVIEW executable and block execution with blockedReason='windows-vi-server-tcp-disabled' when server.tcp.enabled=False is explicitly set, mirroring the Linux labview.conf preflight from VHS-REQ-156. The WindowsLabviewTcpSettings interface exposes a tri-state viServerTcpEnabled (true when enabled or absent — Windows defaults VI Server TCP on; false only on explicit False; 'unknown' when the ini is not readable). The block runs after preflightLinuxHostRuntimeSurface and before preflightWindowsHostRuntimeSurface, so the explicit ini-disabled signal wins over the bitness-conflict surface arm covered by VHS-REQ-621. The lvcompare engine is exempt because it does not connect to LabVIEW VI Server. The preflight does not auto-mutate LabVIEW.ini — write actions race with running LabVIEW IDE rewrites on clean shutdown. The vihs --validate runtime-validation proof serializes the observed host VI Server port (runtime.hostLabviewTcpPort) and its LabVIEW.ini path (runtime.hostLabviewIniPath) so real-hardware evidence proves a non-default server.tcp.port was admitted without a false conflict; the Windows runtime matrix harness port-A scenario derives its expected VI Server port from the selected install's own LabVIEW.ini (the same parse the product uses) rather than a hardcoded or operator-supplied constant, then asserts the admitted run's proof reports hostLabviewIniPath equal to that selected install's ini and hostLabviewTcpPort equal to the port parsed from it — keeping the contract correct for whatever port the operator configures and proving the product read the selected install rather than the latest-used one.

Title: Actionable VI Server Disabled Comparison Guidance
Notes: When a comparison is blocked with windows-vi-server-tcp-disabled or linux-vi-server-tcp-disabled (from the VHS-REQ-623 / VHS-REQ-156 preflights), deriveRuntimeDoctorNextAction emits a VI-Server-specific next-action that names enabling VI Server in LabVIEW (Tools → Options → VI Server) or setting server.tcp.enabled=True (LabVIEW.ini on Windows, labview.conf on Linux), then restarting LabVIEW and rerunning report generation. The next-action becomes the doctor summary's final line so the existing blocked-compare warning notification and history panel runtime result surface the same actionable guidance on both platforms. Detection stays in the compare-time preflights; this requirement owns only the user-facing next-action copy and does not add a pre-panel gate.

Title: Linux Container Bind-Mount Visibility Diagnostic
Notes: When a Linux container comparison fails with labview-cli-invalid-vi-path and the bind-mounted host report directory is outside the user's home directory, buildLinuxContainerBindMountVisibilityNote attaches an actionable diagnostic note naming snap-Docker bind-mount confinement (only the connected home interface is mounted by default) as the likely cause and the remediation (keep report storage under the home directory, or sudo snap connect docker:removable-media; native Docker is unaffected). executeComparisonReport appends the note to the failed run's diagnosticNotes for the linux-container provider only, derived from record.artifactPlan.reportDirectory and the resolved home directory, without changing failureReason or diagnosticReason.

Title: Actionable VI Server Guidance For LabVIEW CLI Connection Failure
Notes: When a host-native LabVIEWCLI compare attempt fails with labview-cli-connection-failed (LabVIEWCLI exit error -350000), classifyRuntimeFailure preserves the -350000 to labview-cli-connection-failed classification and deriveRuntimeDoctorNextAction emits a VI-Server-specific failed-state next-action naming VI Server (TCP/IP) disabled for the selected LabVIEW as the most common cause and the enable path (Tools → Options → VI Server / server.tcp.enabled=True and the configured port), restart LabVIEW, then rerun. Complements VHS-REQ-628 for the post-attempt case the VHS-REQ-623/156 ini preflight cannot catch (absent key, unreadable ini, or written only on clean LabVIEW exit). This requirement owns only the failed-state next-action copy beyond preserving the existing -350000 classification.

Title: Pre-Panel VI Server Prerequisite Gate For VI History Open
Notes: labviewViHistory.open consults the selected host LabVIEW VI Server config after the Git and LabVIEW-CLI gates and refuses to open the panel with a warning toast naming VI Server and the enable path unless server.tcp.enabled=True is explicit. isViServerExplicitlyEnabledInConfig requires an explicit True (case/quote/whitespace tolerant); absent key, False, and unreadable count as not enabled. decideViServerOpenGate allows on not-ready detection, active Docker provider, no resolvable host installation, or non-host platforms; otherwise it reads the Windows LabVIEW.ini adjacent to the selected exe or the Linux labview.conf candidates (reusing the VHS-REQ-156 builder) and blocks unless one is explicitly enabled. Strict open-gate-only rule; the compare-time VHS-REQ-623/156 preflight is unchanged. No TCP port probe. Accepted tradeoff: false-positive block for Windows hosts running VI Server on without an explicit key.

Title: Host LabVIEW Install Catalog Parity
Notes: Activation-time runtime detection (VHS-REQ-616) and the comparison runtime locator (VHS-REQ-155) derive their documented host LabVIEW/LabVIEWCLI/LVCompare install locations from one shared catalog (src/tooling/labviewInstallCatalog.ts) so the lightweight detector recognizes every documented LabVIEW and LabVIEW CLI filesystem install location the locator recognizes, preventing the LabVIEW CLI open gate from false-blocking a host the compare engine can serve. Activation detection resolves the host LabVIEW executable and LabVIEW CLI; LVCompare is a locator-only surface fed by the same catalog. Catalog supplies the supported year range, Linux quarterly (LabVIEW-<year>Q1-64/Q3) plus plain install dirs and shared nilvcli launchers, Windows LabVIEW <year>[ Q1| Q3] folders, the canonical 32-bit shared Windows LabVIEW CLI path, and LVCompare paths. detectLinux/WindowsHostInstallations enumerate the catalog (a quarterly-only Linux host is now detected); buildDocumentedRuntimeCandidates derives the same scan, with the Windows registry query remaining the locator-only superset for non-default installs. Catalog is pure (no VS Code/fs/child-process) so tooling and reporting consume it without a cycle. Activation detection stays filesystem-only; registry-only/custom-path parity is tracked separately.

Title: Manual LabVIEW Runtime Path Override
Notes: viHistorySuite.labviewCliPath and viHistorySuite.labviewExePath let users override host LabVIEW discovery for installs auto-detection does not cover. package.json contributes both as strings and lists both in capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.restrictedConfigurations (they name executables the comparison launches, so untrusted workspaces cannot supply them). readComparisonRuntimeSettings reads both (trimmed; blank -> undefined) into ComparisonRuntimeSettings, so locateComparisonRuntime builds configured candidates and returns configured-labview-cli-path-missing/configured-labview-exe-path-missing for a non-existent path. decideLabviewCliOpenGate allows labviewViHistory.open when a non-empty labviewCliPath is configured, trusting the override (gate stays pure/window-free, no stat); extension.ts passes the configured path. Existence validation stays with the compare-time locator, making the runtime doctor's pre-existing set-the-path guidance functional end to end.

Title: Authoritative Host Fallback For LabVIEW CLI Open Gate
Notes: When the synchronous LabVIEW CLI open gate (VHS-REQ-627) would block labviewViHistory.open from the filesystem-only activation detection (VHS-REQ-616), the open command consults a bounded on-demand authoritative probe before blocking so a Windows registry-resolved / custom-path LabVIEW install the detector cannot see (it never queries the registry) does not false-block. probeWindowsRegistryHostLabviewAvailable reuses the locator's shipped reg query plans+parser and returns true only when a registry-resolved LabVIEW.exe (named directly, or derived from the National Instruments install-directory Path value the stock NI registry actually records) exists on disk AND the shared Windows LabVIEW CLI exists on disk; it performs no container/process probes and never throws. decideLabviewCliOpenGateWithRegistryFallback returns the base decision unless it is block on Windows with a probe supplied, then allows when the probe reports available (fail-closed to the base block on throw). extension.ts awaits the fallback with the registry probe only on the block branch. The synchronous decideLabviewCliOpenGate contract (VHS-REQ-627/629/633) is unchanged; activation detection stays filesystem-only.

Title: Selected-File On-Demand Eligibility

Title: Pre-Panel LabVIEW Bitness Conflict Gate For VI History Open
Notes: labviewViHistory.open consults a bounded Windows-only running-process bitness observation after the VI Server gate (VHS-REQ-631) and refuses to open the panel with a plain-language toast naming the running and selected LabVIEW year/bitness when an observed LabVIEW.exe bitness differs from viHistorySuite.labviewBitness; the toast offers a Pick Runtime Provider action invoking labviewViHistory.pickRuntimeProvider. decideBitnessOpenGate fails open on unavailable detection, non-Windows, Docker provider, no host install, unknown or matching bitness, or observation error. Compare-time VHS-REQ-621 detection and classification is unchanged.

Title: Pre-Panel LabVIEW Version Mismatch Gate For VI History Open

Matching-version sessions remain admitted; compare-time VHS-REQ-621 and VHS-REQ-155 are unchanged.

This provides the post-Compare re-entry path without broadening the explorer/editor context-menu when-clause, which stays resourceExtname-scoped (VHS-REQ-004 unchanged).

Title: Commit Body In History Panel

No regression of VHS-REQ-007 NUL/control-safe parsing, VHS-REQ-008 bounded queries, VHS-REQ-017 escaping, or VHS-REQ-133 explicit compare selection.

Title: Self-Contained Single-File Comparison Report Output
Notes: Comparison reports are generated as a self-contained single-file HTML (-ReportType htmlsinglefile) with difference images embedded as data URIs, eliminating the per-image webview sub-requests that previously exhausted the resource loader on large reports and left images showing their path text. Applied uniformly across host-native, Linux container, and Windows container providers. Newly generated reports need no sibling <report>_files assets directory; previously retained multi-file reports still render via the interim lazy-image-loading path.

Title: Working-Tree (Uncommitted) Comparison Against a Prior Revision
Notes: Detects uncommitted working-tree changes to a tracked VI (git status --porcelain scoped to the path) and lets the user compare the on-disk file against the newest commit (HEAD) via a reserved WORKTREE revision sentinel. The sentinel side reads bytes from disk instead of git show, and the selected-revision tree materializer stages the base commit tree as dependency context. A VI with one commit plus uncommitted changes becomes eligible. Working-tree comparisons are read-only. Phase 3 (issue #1366) retains a working-tree comparison when it produces a content-addressed snapshot identity: it is archived under a content-addressed pair-ID (WORKTREE:<snapshotId>), appended to a persisted per-VI worktree-snapshot-index@v1 retention index (worktreeSnapshotIndex.ts) with a keep-last-N limit (viHistorySuite.comparison.worktreeSnapshotRetentionLimit, default 5, 0 disables), and surfaced in the dashboard as a non-reproducible uncommitted snapshot entry; evicted snapshots' archive dirs are garbage-collected. A run that produced no snapshot identity (blocked/daemon-down) stays unarchived. The history panel pins a selectable working-tree row so the on-disk version can be paired with any committed revision (not only HEAD).

Title: Docker Daemon Not Running Comparison Toast
Notes: When a comparison blocks because the Docker daemon is unreachable (dockerDaemonReachable=false and dockerCliAvailable!=false, i.e. the CLI is not confirmed absent: true or undefined) under blockedReason docker-provider-unavailable/docker-only-provider-unavailable/auto-docker-installed-provider-unavailable, isDockerDaemonNotRunningBlock returns true. The !=false CLI check mirrors the doctor next-action partition in deriveContainerRecoveryAction (dockerCliAvailable=false steers to install Docker; any other state with an unreachable daemon steers to start Docker Desktop), so the concise toast fires for the real-world dockerCliAvailable=undefined shape instead of leaking the verbose toast and auto-opened report; the daemon side stays strict so dockerDaemonReachable=undefined returns false. The action surfaces dockerCliAvailable/dockerDaemonReachable plus the selected platform and outcome blocked-docker-daemon-not-running, and suppresses the report webview unless archiving genuinely failed (archiveFailureReason=retained-archive-write-failed), falling through to open the webview directly only on a real archive write failure so diagnostics are never lost. A working-tree comparison intentionally not archived (VHS-REQ-641, archiveFailureReason=retained-archive-unavailable, retainedArchiveAvailable=false) is still suppressed because the guard keys on the genuine write-failure reason rather than retainedArchiveAvailable, fixing the leaked auto-opened report tab for daemon-down working-tree compares. openViHistoryCommand shows a single platform-aware toast built by buildDockerDaemonNotRunningMessage (Docker Desktop on win32, the Docker daemon otherwise) with Retry (re-run same pair) and Show diagnostics (open retained packet) instead of the verbose runtime warning. All other blocked and failed reasons keep their existing diagnostics surface.

Title: Docker Not Installed Comparison Toast
Notes: Sibling of VHS-REQ-642 for the Docker-not-installed case (dockerCliAvailable=false) under blockedReason docker-provider-unavailable/docker-only-provider-unavailable/auto-docker-installed-provider-unavailable: isDockerNotInstalledBlock returns true (mutually exclusive with the daemon-down predicate on dockerCliAvailable); the action returns outcome blocked-docker-not-installed and suppresses the report webview unless archiving genuinely failed (archiveFailureReason=retained-archive-write-failed), falling through to open the webview directly only on a real archive write failure so diagnostics are never lost. A working-tree comparison intentionally not archived (VHS-REQ-641, retained-archive-unavailable) is still suppressed. openViHistoryCommand shows a single platform-aware toast built by buildDockerNotInstalledMessage (Docker Desktop on win32, Docker otherwise) with Install Docker (opens INSTALL_DOCKER_URL via openExternal) and Show diagnostics (open retained packet) instead of the verbose runtime warning. No automatic install or process launch; link only. The VHS-REQ-642 daemon-down toast and all other blocked/failed reasons are unchanged.

Title: Commit Body In Comparison Report
Notes: The produced comparison report renders the full Git commit body (git format %b) for both the selected and base revision context cards alongside the existing date/author/subject facts: in the retained packet HTML (and therefore the VHS-REQ-626 packet export, which copies that HTML), the in-panel shared panel context markup, and the exported generated-report copy. Per VHS-REQ-626, generated-report export injects revision context into the exported copy only while leaving the retained LabVIEW-generated source report unchanged. The body is carried through ComparisonReportRevisionMetadata from the in-memory retained-history commits already passed to comparison generation (no new Git reads, no regression of VHS-REQ-008), rendered HTML-escaped with multi-line preserved (no regression of VHS-REQ-017). Undefined (not-retained) metadata renders the shared not-retained fallback; a retained empty/whitespace body (including the synthesized working-tree revision, VHS-REQ-641) renders a distinct empty-body fallback. Reuses the VHS-REQ-639 history-panel commit-body pattern; history-panel and review-packet body rendering and comparison runtime behavior are unchanged.

Title: Configurable Comparison Report Flags
Notes: The LabVIEW comparison report difference-suppression filters are user- and workspace-configurable through native VS Code settings under viHistorySuite.report.*: boolean filters ignoreViAttributes ignoreFrontPanel ignoreFrontPanelObjectPosition ignoreBlockDiagram and ignoreBlockDiagramCosmetic. readComparisonReportOptions reads them at the comparison-report action boundary and threads them through buildComparisonReportExecutionPlan into buildLabviewCliCreateComparisonReportPlan; each enabled filter emits exactly its verified LabVIEWCLI CreateComparisonReport flag (-noattr -nofp -nofppos -nobd -nobdcosm). The report output format is fixed to single-file HTML (-ReportType htmlsinglefile, hardcoded in the CLI plan) and is NOT configurable: there is no viHistorySuite.report.format setting and no panel format control (#545), so the multi-file html report type cannot be reintroduced for newly generated reports (no regression of VHS-REQ-640). With nothing configured the generated invocation is identical to the prior hardcoded single-file HTML compare-everything behavior. The settings render in the native Settings editor with no scripted webview and the comparison-report panel keeps scripts disabled (no regression of VHS-REQ-626). The Runtime & Report Settings panel (openRuntimeReportPanelCommand with the runtimeReportPanel renderer) surfaces these flags as Include checkboxes (checked = include the difference class); applyComparisonReportOptionSelection persists each edit to viHistorySuite.report.* with the Include-to-ignore inversion so unchecking a class writes ignore=true.

Title: LabVIEW Container Image Tag Model
Notes: Pure parser/formatter/comparator for nationalinstruments/labview <year>q<quarter>[patch<n>]-<platform> tags; namespace-pinned and newest-first ordered with a higher patch newer and the base release oldest within its group; performs no I/O.

Title: Published Container Image Tag Discovery
Notes: Anonymous read-only bounded Docker Hub tag discovery filtered to platform and the supported year floor through the VHS-REQ-646 model behind an injected fetch boundary with a bounded HTTPS default; failure degrades to empty plus a non-fatal note and never throws.

Title: Local Container Image Tag Discovery
Notes: Enumerates locally pulled nationalinstruments/labview images via an injected docker images boundary and merges with published results marking local presence and registry publication; offline-safe and empty when the Docker CLI is absent. The default lister distinguishes three Docker states: CLI absent (spawn error) resolves empty (nothing pulled); CLI present but daemon unreachable (non-zero exit) rejects; success (exit 0) resolves the parsed list. On a lister rejection discoverLocalContainerImageVersions sets localPresenceUnknown and returns empty with a note so consumers report local presence as unknown rather than empty; a resolved empty list does not set the flag.

Title: Container Image Version Selection Setting And Quick-Pick
Notes: Contributes the trust-restricted viHistorySuite.container.imageVersion setting and the labviewViHistory.pickContainerImageVersion command listing discovered versions newest-first with pulled-locally vs available-to-pull annotations and persisting the chosen tag at Global scope; trusted-workspace gated with a Clear option and an actionable empty-discovery message. When local presence is unknown because the Docker engine was offline (localPresenceUnknown from VHS-REQ-648), non-local versions are annotated Local presence unknown (Docker engine offline) instead of Available to pull in both the quick-pick (buildContainerImageVersionItems) and the runtime settings panel (presenceLabel), so a pulled image is never misreported as needing a pull while the daemon is down.

Title: Selected Container Version Drives Both Providers With Fail-Closed Resolution
Notes: The locator resolves the selected container image version to a concrete reference for both windows-container and linux-container providers with an explicit full-string override still taking precedence and bypasses the legacy docker-provider-labview-version-not-implemented year pin when a version is selected; unset preserves the prior platform default and a selected-but-unacquirable image fails closed through the existing container-image acquisition path. A selected version whose platform conflicts with the active Docker container host mode fails closed with the classified container-image-platform-mismatch blocked reason instead of silently substituting the platform default. The mismatch compare-time block surfaces a concise toast naming the selected image container platform vs the active Docker engine mode (no provider/rejected-provider internals and no host-native clause) with a Pick Image Version action and suppresses the auto-opened report while still persisting the packet (#532). The image-version picker surfaces a stale cross-platform selection as a leading warning Clear row. The mismatch remediation is delivered through the toast action and the labviewViHistory.pickContainerImageVersion command; the minimized History panel no longer renders an in-panel Pick Image Version CTA or compare-preflight section.

Title: Chain Container Image Version Pick After Docker Provider Selection
Notes: The Runtime & Report Settings panel co-locates the LabVIEW container image version selector with the runtime provider selection: the container section (openRuntimeReportPanelCommand with the runtimeReportPanel renderer) is shown when Docker is the selected or available provider so choosing Docker surfaces the image-version control inline instead of chaining a separate quick-pick. selectContainerVersion persists the chosen tag or clears to the newest supported default in viHistorySuite.container.imageVersion via applyContainerImageVersionSelection; discovery reuses the published and local image catalog boundaries behind injected fetch and list seams. The standalone labviewViHistory.pickContainerImageVersion command stays registered for the compare-preflight remediation CTAs but is removed from the Command Palette.

Title: Live Container Image Pull Progress
Notes: acquireWindowsContainerImage drives the LabVIEW image cold-pull through the Docker Engine API POST /images/create stream over the local daemon socket (Windows named pipe or Linux /var/run/docker.sock) and aggregates per-layer progressDetail.current/total byte counts into a monotonic clamped 0-100 percent with downloaded/total byte figures surfaced in the acquisition progress message. The Engine API path is attempted only where the daemon socket is directly reachable (native Windows or Linux-native); the Linux-to-Windows-docker WSL bridge and any other host fall back to the prior docker pull CLI acquisition so behavior is never worse. An unreachable socket transparently falls back to the CLI; an in-band pull error or non-2xx daemon response is a failed acquisition carrying the error. Read-only anonymous pull of the namespace-pinned nationalinstruments/labview repository with no registry credential header and no new dependency (Node http.request over the socket). Parser and aggregator are pure; the daemon-socket request is behind an injected boundary so the feature is unit-testable on Linux.

Title: Stable Byte-Percentage Pull Progress
Notes: Before the cold-pull begins the extension resolves the image total compressed download size from the Docker Hub registry manifest (anonymous pull token from auth.docker.io then the manifest from registry-1.docker.io; a manifest list or OCI image index is resolved to the windows/amd64 manifest) and sums the per-layer compressed sizes. The pull-progress aggregator divides downloaded bytes by that stable total instead of the partially-known live-stream totals, crediting cached Already exists layers from a per-layer size map so a partial cache still reaches the total; the percent stays monotonic and capped below 100 and the toast shows downloaded over total bytes (for example 42% (8.1 GB / 19.3 GB)). When the stable total is unavailable (non-Docker-Hub registry, auth or network or parse error, timeout, or missing platform) progress falls back to the layer-weighted figure of VHS-REQ-654 so behavior is never worse. Resolution is anonymous with no credentials, bounded by a per-request timeout and a response-size cap, and contacts only the fixed Docker Hub registry and token hosts derived from the image reference so there is no SSRF surface. The reference, challenge, and manifest helpers are pure and the HTTP request is behind an injected boundary so the resolver is unit-testable on Linux without network.

Title: Container Image Pull Phase Signaling
Notes: The pull-progress parser distinguishes the per-layer lifecycle states Downloading, Download complete, Extracting, Pull complete, and Already exists, and the aggregator derives an overall phase (preparing then downloading then extracting then complete) plus a layer-weighted extraction percentage. The acquisition message names the current phase: a pulling message with the download percentage while downloading, an extracting message with its own percentage and completed over total layer count while extracting (for example Extracting container image: image 60% (8/13 layers)), and a finalizing message once every layer is pulled before the existing Container image ready signal. The progress bar advances monotonically through both phases (download owns the larger share and extraction the remainder) so it does not freeze at the download ceiling during the multi-minute unpack. Extraction signaling is robust when the daemon omits Extracting byte detail because the extraction percentage still advances as layers reach Pull complete. The download-phase behavior of VHS-REQ-654 and VHS-REQ-655 is unchanged.

Title: Version-Aware LabVIEW Container Execution
Notes: resolveLinuxContainerLabviewProfile derives the in-container LabVIEW executable and headless mechanism from the selected Linux image year: 2026 Q1 and later use LabVIEW-<year>-64/labviewprofull with -Headless, while 2025 Q3 and earlier use LabVIEW-<year>-64/labview with an exported EnableCICDFeaturesForLabVIEW=TRUE and no -Headless (per ni/labview-for-containers). An unparseable image falls back to the LabVIEW 2026 profile. buildLinuxContainerCommandPlan threads the profile through the LabVIEWCLI args, the container bash script, and the LVCompare lvpath; the container comparison runs a single attempt with no orchestrator-level headless-session-reset retry (the resolved headless mechanism is applied as selected). The locator no longer emits docker-provider-labview-version-not-implemented (the legacy 2026 pin is removed); the resolved image governs the version and the labview-version-unsupported-for-comparison-report floor still applies. The runtime doctor Requested runtime line reports the image-derived year for container providers. The Docker provider option is labeled Docker with no version or bitness in both the picker and the Runtime & Report Settings panel; selecting it persists runtimeProvider=docker and clears labviewVersion and labviewBitness; isPersistedSelectionSatisfiable, the activation seed completeness, selectActiveRuntime, and the runtime panel selection treat a Docker selection as complete with the provider key alone, and the status-bar label stays image-based. The panel LabVIEW container image section is shown only when Docker is the comparison runtime (persisted docker, or unset with an auto-detected Docker active provider) and hidden for a host selection, coordinating with VHS-REQ-651. Windows-container execution remains LabVIEW 2026 pinned and the vihs terminal CLI docker prompt is unchanged.

Title: Source Control Semantic Change Hover
Notes: Source Control file decoration surfaces the cached semantic what-changed narrative for a changed VI gated on workspace trust.

Title: Single-VI Interactive Preview Rendering
Notes: Single-VI preview renders one LabVIEW VI to a self-contained HTML document via NI's PrintToSingleFileHtml custom LabVIEWCLI operation (vendored under resources/labview-cli-operations/PrintToSingleFileHtml from ni/labview-for-containers), so a selected revision can be inspected without a second revision to compare. buildLabviewCliPrintToSingleFileHtmlPlan builds the host command with -VI/-OutputPath/-AdditionalOperationDirectory and default -LogToConsole TRUE/-c/-o, emitting -LabVIEWPath/-PortNumber/-Headless only when supplied and never the two-VI CreateComparisonReport flags. rewriteViPreviewArgsForLinuxContainerWorkspace maps the VI and output to workspace-relative container paths, repoints the operation directory at the read-only mount, swaps in the in-container LabVIEW executable, and keeps -Headless once. buildLinuxContainerViPreviewCommandPlan assembles a shell-less docker run with the workspace and read-only operation mounts and a single bash -lc script that hardens VI Server in the per-version LabVIEW config and runs the CLI exactly once (single-cycle, no cold-launch -350000 retry), matching the comparison runtime recipe. This first slice is the pure command-plan layer; execution orchestration, the preview webview, and the single-selection and custom-editor triggers land in later slices on the same feature branch. The renderer runs headless on the LabVIEW Linux container without the Web Services wsapi image-to-PNG dependency that breaks the gpreview alternative.

Title: On-Demand VI Semantic PR Review Workflow
Notes: Maintainer-dispatched workflow_dispatch workflow that delegates to a reusable workflow_call unit (vi-semantic-pr-review-callable.yml) so any LabVIEW repo can consume it. Runs the shipped runViSemanticPrReview CLI against any target repo/PR on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner (pulling the NI LabVIEW docker image) and upserts a sticky VI review comment on the target PR by hidden marker. Fails closed to trusted vi-history-suite refs (enforce_trusted_ref gate); posts cross-repo via the VI_REVIEW_TARGET_TOKEN secret passed as GH_TOKEN (the workflow's own GITHUB_TOKEN cannot comment on a different target repo); resolves the review range as merge-base(base,head); passes the canonical <version>-linux container tag; verifies docker and pulls the NI LabVIEW image as a fail-fast gate; uploads review-out artifact; contains no vagrant reference (VHS-REQ-599).

Title: VI Semantic Comparison Model And Agent MCP Surface
Notes: Versioned vi-semantic-comparison@v1 model plus a shared what-changed narrative, the open Draft-07 JSON-Schema standard (comparison/history/repository-index) with an offline subset validator, and a dependency-free JSON-RPC MCP server exposing eight agent tools that VS Code registers for Copilot agent mode. Model, schemas, handler, and orchestrators stay VS Code- and network-free and are reused by the Source Control hover (VHS-REQ-660) and the PR-review workflow (VHS-REQ-661).

Title: Preview And Comparison Cache Warming On VI Change
Notes: On VI change under the Docker runtime the extension warms that VI's preview render cache and runs a background HEAD-versus-working-tree comparison whose report records the semantic narrative so the Source Control hover updates; each change is dispatched immediately (no debounce) and warms are single-flight serialized; opt-in via viHistorySuite.preview.warmOnChange with preview.enabled gating the preview warm and workspace trust gating the comparison warm.

Title: Win32 Host-Native Headless Comparison For 32-bit LabVIEW Parity
Notes: When the opt-in LV_RTE_WIN_HOSTNATIVE_HEADLESS=1 toggle is set and the extension runs natively on Windows against a host-native labview-cli comparison, buildWindowsHostNativeHeadlessCommandPlan wraps the bare CLI plan in a powershell -EncodedCommand headless launch script that prelaunches the selected LabVIEW --headless (binding the VI Server without an interactive desktop), tunes the LabVIEWCLI.ini connect window, runs the CLI verbatim exactly once (single-cycle, no cold-launch retry), reusing the windows-container launch technique so a non-interactive session can drive a real comparison against locally installed 32-bit LabVIEW 2026 (the bitness the x64-only windows-container provider cannot exercise). prepareExecutionContext applies the wrap only when processPlatform is win32, the effective runtime platform is win32, and the toggle is set; the default interactive host-native path is unchanged; the shared builder keeps byte-identical windows-container output. The Vagrant lane exercising this is a local maintainer helper only, never a CI gate.

Title: Mandatory Local Vagrant Release Attestation
Notes: Kicking off a marketplace release requires a fresh local Vagrant Windows/LabVIEW validation attestation for the exact release version. checkReleaseReadiness.js --require-release-attestation appends a gating release-attestation check that passes only when a releaseGating track in the committed runtime-validation ledger has lastValidatedVersion equal to the release version (absent/stale fails closed; --strict exits nonzero). Default advisory readiness stays three checks plus the display-only runtime line (VHS-REQ-615.13). The marketplace-release workflow runs the gate before publish by reading the committed ledger so hosted CI needs no hypervisor and the workflow YAML names no Vagrant helper (VHS-REQ-599 alignment). npm run vagrant:validate:release runs the lane and records the attestation via recordRuntimeValidation.js. Under --require-release-attestation the gate also appends a CI-safe box-manifest-integrity check that fails closed unless the committed vagrant/box-manifest.json is present, schema-valid, and carries a non-empty recordedForVersion (the box is sha256-identified and regenerated only when rebuilt, so an unchanged box does not block a version bump; attestation freshness is enforced by release-attestation). A box-provenance-binding check fails closed when a release-gating track records a boxSha256 that does not equal the committed manifest sha256 (absent boxSha256 soft-passes). Reads the committed manifest only; byte hashing stays in verifyVagrantBox.cjs --verify.

Title: Versioned Dev-Tools GitHub Release Channel
Notes: The development toolset is distributable as a versioned content-addressed GitHub Release artifact independent of the marketplace. docs/devtools-release.manifest.json is the committed source of truth for the bundled files; buildDevToolsRelease.js emits a deterministic contentDigest and a provenance manifest binding the toolset to its requirements state; --pack produces a reproducible POSIX ustar+gzip tarball via Node built-ins; verifyDevToolsRelease.js fails closed on tamper/missing/self-verify; devtools-release.yml builds, self-verifies, dedups on the content digest, defaults dispatch to a dry run, maps develop to prerelease and main to stable, and names no Vagrant helper (VHS-REQ-599).

Title: Independent SemVer Dev-Tools Version Line
Notes: Independent SemVer 2.0 dev-tools version line (devtools-vX.Y.Z), decoupled from the extension Marketplace version. Dependency-free semver util (src/support/semver.ts + scripts/lib/semver.cjs mirror: parse/validate/compare with prerelease + build-metadata precedence, no npm dep). docs/devtools-release.manifest.json carries a committed `version` source of truth; buildDevToolsRelease.js fails closed when it is missing/non-semver and emits it in the vi-history-suite/devtools-release@v1 provenance packet + JSON Schema required list. devtools-release.yml tags devtools-v<version> (stable) / devtools-v<version>-dev.<run> (prerelease), guards packet==manifest version, dedup/prune scoped by devtools-v* prefix + prerelease flag. Foundation for VHS-REQ-677 runtime pinning; extends VHS-REQ-667.

Title: Runtime Dev-Tools Version Pinning For The MCP Server
Notes: Extension pins and runtime-consumes an independent dev-tools version (devtools-vX.Y.Z from VHS-REQ-676) for its MCP server launch without a Marketplace republish. viHistorySuite.devTools.version (bundled default | devtools-vX.Y.Z) normalizes fail-closed; viHistorySuite.devTools.checkForUpdates opt-in (default off). devToolsResolver.ts (IO/network injected) resolves the MCP launch: bundled from extension out/, pinned from <globalStorage>/devtools/<version>/ only when trusted AND integrity-verified else fails closed to bundled. installDevToolsRelease selects exact tag, downloads archive+manifest, verifies per-file sha256 + aggregate contentDigest (VHS-REQ-676 scheme), marks verified on success, removes partial installs on any failure. Opt-in check surfaces only newer STABLE versions via VHS-REQ-676 semver compare. Fixed stale dev-tools VSIX doc mention. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013; builds on VHS-REQ-676/667.

Title: Supply-Chain State Read-Model
Notes: Read-only aggregator (npm run supply-chain:state) reporting the provenance state of every shipped artifact bound to a committed digest in one vi-history-suite/supply-chain-state@v1 packet: box manifest, runtime-validation ledger, requirements manifest, and dev-tools toolset content digest. Each artifact reports availability, whether it gates a release, its digest, a tri-state freshness vs the current build, and a drift reason; runtime enumerates per-track freshness. Rolls up status attention when any release-gating artifact is unavailable/stale else fresh; --strict is an opt-in local signal not wired into CI. Release-readiness exposes an opt-in --require-supply-chain-fresh gate that promotes the read-model to a hard check and fails closed. Reads existing ledgers/manifests only and mutates no source.

Title: Serialized Local VI Server Acquisition
Notes: In-process serialization primitive (createLocalViServerAcquisitionLock) that grants a per-key FIFO single-flight slot keyed by the local VI Server endpoint (localViServerLockKey from provider + derived server.tcp.port, default token when absent), so concurrent host-native LabVIEWCLI launches against the same endpoint take turns instead of racing the one VI Server. The host-native branch of executeViPreview acquires the slot before launching and releases it in a finally for every outcome; the release is idempotent; container/docker runs never acquire a slot and distinct endpoints never block each other. The host-native comparison path is the documented next adopter of the same shared lock. Each external LabVIEW invocation is treated as one cycle of a single-cycle timed loop (single attempt, no retry) and measured by createCycleMeter for per-cycle duration, monotonic cycle count, and inter-cycle latency; executeViPreview attaches the render cycle measurement to its result.

Title: Release State Read-Model And Gated Publish Authority
Notes: Read-only aggregator (npm run release:state) emitting a vi-history-suite/release-state@v1 packet: durable ground-truth stages develop-ready/tagged/on-main/published/backsynced (reached true|false|null), furthest stage, stageGaps, and a gated single-principal authority posture (one principal dispatches and approves; the protected marketplace-release environment enforces the manual-approval step). Rollup status attention when authority definitively incomplete or a stage gap exists else ready; --strict exits nonzero. All git/gh/vsce boundaries injected; main and develop refs configurable; backsynced derived from the develop tip; a default pinned vsce show reader resolves published. Release-readiness adds a --release-context-only release-authority hard check (fails closed on incomplete authority, passes-with-note when unverified; not coupled to --require-release-attestation) and the marketplace-release workflow runs buildReleaseState.js --strict as a fail-closed guard.

Title: Headless Preview-Cache Worker
Notes: Headless preview-cache worker CLI (npm run preview:cache:warm) so a Codespace/CI runner/Docker host generates and stores single-VI preview caches for a whole workspace without VS Code. listWorkspaceViFiles enumerates .vi/.vit/.vim/.ctl via injected fs (skips node_modules/.git/out/dist/.vscode-test, depth-bounded, sorted, optional limit). runViPreviewCacheWarm resolves the Docker preview runtime once (blocked packet on failure), warms every VI serially through warmViPreviewCache with a file-backed cache at --cache-dir, and emits a self-describing vi-history-suite/preview-cache-warm@v1 packet with a per-entry manifest (repo-relative path, content-addressed cache key, outcome rendered/cache-hit/failed/blocked, bytes, inline-image count). renderViPreviewForFile now returns the cache key it used so the manifest maps key->VI path. CLI requires --cache-dir (fail-closed remedy), supports --json/--output (path-safe)/--include-provenance, exits nonzero on block or any render failure. Producer slice of the preview-cache fabric; reuses VHS-REQ-659 warm loop + cache.

Title: Preview-Cache Health Read-Model
Notes: Read-only preview-cache coverage read-model (npm run preview:cache:health) emitting a vi-history-suite/preview-cache-health@v1 packet. buildViPreviewCacheHealth compares the current workspace VI enumeration, a prior vi-history-suite/preview-cache-warm@v1 manifest, and the cache directory's present <key>.html files, classifying each VI cached/stale/missing/failed with totals (cached/stale/missing/failed/orphanedCacheFiles/removedVis/coveragePercent) + per-VI entries + orphanedCacheKeys + removedViPaths + healthy. Pure/injectable; CLI requires --cache-dir (fail-closed), optional --manifest, --json/--output(path-safe)/--strict (exit 1 when not fully healthy). Observability slice of the preview-cache fabric; reuses VHS-REQ-671 manifest + workspace enumerator.

Title: Portable Preview-Cache Bundle
Notes: Portable content-addressed preview-cache bundle (npm run preview:cache:bundle). buildViPreviewCacheBundleManifest emits a vi-history-suite/preview-cache-bundle@v1 manifest (per-entry content key + sha256 integrity digest + VI paths, sorted, dedup, provenance); verifyViPreviewCacheBundle detects tampered/missing docs; planViPreviewCacheBundleImport plans a lossless content-addressed merge (skip-present/reject-integrity-mismatch/add). CLI bundle exports a cache dir to a bundle directory (manifest.json + <key>.html, optional --manifest VI-path annotation + --source), unbundle verifies and merges into --into target (fail-closed on not-found/integrity-failed). Pure model + fs-wiring CLI. Portability slice of the preview-cache fabric; reuses VHS-REQ-659 content key + VHS-REQ-671 warm manifest.

Title: Preview-Cache Exchange
Notes: Preview-cache exchange (npm run preview:cache:exchange) publishing/fetching portable bundles via content-addressed GitHub Releases, reusing the dev-tools release-channel transport (VHS-REQ-667). Pure planning: computeBundleContentDigest + deriveExchangeReleaseTag (preview-cache-<12hex>), planExchangePublish (publish/skip-existing/skip-empty, idempotent), selectExchangeReleaseToFetch (explicit tag or most-recent). CLI publish packs a bundle dir to tar.gz + gh release create (skip if tag exists), fetch downloads+extracts+verifies+losslessly merges into --into target (reuses bundle verify+import), fail-closed on missing release/archive/integrity. gh/tar/fs boundaries injected. Distribution slice of the preview-cache fabric; reuses VHS-REQ-672 bundle.

Title: Preview-Cache Generation Fleet
Notes: Reusable sharded cache-generation fleet (preview-cache-fleet-callable.yml + maintainer dispatch wrapper preview-cache-fleet.yml). plan computes a bounded 1..32 shard matrix, render (matrix) warms each disjoint --shard i/n slice into a cache and bundles it, merge combines the shard bundles (content-addressed dedup) and publishes to the exchange (VHS-REQ-673) only when publish=true (default dry-run uploads artifacts). selectWorkspaceViShard (round-robin, disjoint, union==input) + worker --shard flag. Trusted-ref guarded, tool checkout SHA-pinned to job.workflow_sha, no vagrant (VHS-REQ-599). Scale slice + capstone of the preview-cache fabric; reuses VHS-REQ-671 worker + VHS-REQ-672 bundle + VHS-REQ-673 exchange + VHS-REQ-661 reusable-workflow pattern.

Title: Marketplace Pre-Release Channel
Notes: Marketplace release workflow publishes to the stable or pre-release channel selected from the release tag minor-version parity (odd minor = pre-release, even = stable, per the VS Code convention). Determine Release Channel step (after Verify Package Version, before publish) derives channel + pre_release outputs; Publish To Marketplace passes vsce --pre-release only on the pre-release channel, still one step gated by the idempotent pre-publish check. Optional workflow_dispatch channel input (stable|prerelease, empty=derive) must agree with the parity-derived channel or the run fails closed. All VHS-REQ-609/670 guards (protected environment approval, exact vX.Y.Z tag, package==tag, origin/main reachability, release-state --strict, runtime attestation, supply-chain freshness, bounded listing verification + retained evidence) apply unchanged to both channels; no automatic trigger. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-016; builds on VHS-REQ-609/670.

Title: Runtime Dev-Tools Install Lifecycle
Notes: Runtime filesystem/network boundary + commands that install/uninstall/update-check a pinned dev-tools version (VHS-REQ-677) without a Marketplace republish. devToolsInstaller.ts (dependency-free, injected HTTP/fs): lists devtools-v* releases from the OFFICIAL repo over HTTPS, downloads the tarball + devtools-release.json, extracts the deterministic ustar+gzip archive with node zlib + a small ustar parser (no tar dep), rejects path-traversal entries, folds the aggregate content digest identically to scripts/buildDevToolsRelease.js, and manages installed versions (list verified-marker installs, uninstall one). devToolsRuntime.ts orchestrates installPinnedDevTools, uninstallDevTools (warns when removing the pinned version), and the opt-in stable-only update check (no network unless enabled + pinned + trusted; swallows network errors). extension.ts registers labviewViHistory.installPinnedDevTools + labviewViHistory.uninstallDevTools, runs the activation update check, and surfaces an actionable install notification on a pinned-install-missing MCP fallback. Integrity-verified before use, official-source-only, workspace-trust-gated, fail-closed. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013; builds on VHS-REQ-676/677.

Title: Dev-Tools Status Command And Consumer Documentation
Notes: Read-only labviewViHistory.showDevToolsStatus command + consumer docs for the dev-tools pinning lifecycle. reportDevToolsStatus (VS Code-free, injected listInstalledVersions) reports the pinned viHistorySuite.devTools.version, whether it is installed+integrity-verified, which build the MCP server launches (bundled vs pinned; pin active only once installed), the verified installed versions, and the checkForUpdates flag; mutates nothing and degrades a malformed setting to bundled. docs/devtools-release.md documents pinning a version in the extension, the install/uninstall/status commands, the opt-in update check, workspace-trust gating, and fail-closed fallback; docs/mcp-server.md notes the pinned-build launch. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013; builds on VHS-REQ-677/679.

Title: Agent Operating Control-Plane Capability
Notes: Parent capability for the agent operating control-plane (epic #2144): exposes live repository ground-truth to agents through read-only schema-versioned read-models so behavior is driven by verifiable current state, not stale docs. Read surfaces require live GitHub authorization and fail closed when absent rather than degrading to defaults; acting (write) surfaces are governed and default-disabled under VHS-REQ-696. Grown read-first behind a stable schema. First surface is the VHS-REQ-692 repo-truth read-model.

Title: Repo-Truth Read-Model
Notes: Read-only aggregator (npm run repo:truth) emitting one self-describing vi-history-suite/repo-truth-read-model@v1 packet spanning governance domains (slice 1: merge-queue policy, coverage, requirement health). The merge-queue domain extracts min-entries-to-merge, wait minutes, grouping strategy, and merge method from the branch merge_queue ruleset rule (present:false when absent). FAILS CLOSED on GitHub auth: missing/unauthenticated gh exits nonzero with an actionable message and emits no packet, never degrading to defaults; sibling read-model domains degrade to available:false on local failure. text/json/markdown/schema output modes; --schema publishes the JSON Schema with no gh call. Reuses lib/schemaEnvelope + lib/outputContract; reads only, mutates nothing, gates nothing. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013 under VHS-REQ-691.

Title: Agent Environment Consistency Gate
Notes: Git hooks keeping a local working environment consistent after merge/checkout (epic #2144, agent efficiency). checkEnvSync.js evaluates env-sync facts into problems + a hard-stale verdict where ONLY node_modules-vs-lockfile mismatch is hard; missing/stale out and changed requirements are advisory. node_modules staleness is CONTENT-based: sha256(package-lock.json) vs a git-ignored install marker recorded under node_modules/ by the npm prepare lifecycle, immune to git checkout/reset mtime churn. pre-commit fails closed on hard-stale; post-merge/post-checkout report synchronously and always exit 0 (git ignores their exit code). installGitHooks.js (npm prepare) idempotently sets core.hooksPath=.githooks and no-ops outside a git work-tree. --no-verify bypass cannot be prevented at hook level; forbidden by policy not technical guarantee. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013.

Title: Repo-Governance MCP Server
Notes: Dependency-free JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio MCP server (npm run repo:governance:mcp), separate from the VI semantic-comparison MCP, exposing the repo-truth read-model (VHS-REQ-692) to MCP clients as a single read-only get_repo_truth tool that returns the packet as text content. Handles initialize/tools-list/ping/notifications; reuses the read-model in process (dependency-free, vscode-free); the read-model fail-closed-on-auth posture propagates as a JSON-RPC application error rather than a fabricated packet. Read-only: no write/acting surface (those are governed and default-disabled under VHS-REQ-696). Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013 under VHS-REQ-691.

Title: Control-Plane Read-Model Publishing Workflow
Notes: Read-only GitHub Actions workflow (Repo-Truth Read-Model) that generates the repo-truth read-model JSON with a live GITHUB_TOKEN (so the fail-closed-on-auth domains resolve) and uploads it as a repo-truth-read-model artifact. Runs on manual dispatch + daily schedule, never on push; least-privilege contents:read with no write scope; mutates nothing and gates nothing. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013 under VHS-REQ-691.

Title: Governed Control-Plane Write Path
Notes: Fail-closed, default-disabled governed write path (the control-plane's single acting surface). A committed control-plane-write.json enablement flag gates all writes; missing/malformed config fails closed to disabled. authorizeWrite refuses when disabled or the tier is off; Tier 1 board-sync needs the flag but no per-action approval, other tiers require a server-verified allowlisted approver. The pure planner mirrors only directly-verified truth (linked PR merged => Done/Proven) and never infers; the executor applies + append-logs only when authorized. Ships DISABLED. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013 under VHS-REQ-691; ADR-0020.

Title: Control-Plane Board-Sync Shadow Mode
Notes: Shadow-mode board-sync (observability precursor to VHS-REQ-696): reads live directly-verifiable truth (project board field values + which tracked items are closed/merged) and computes, via the same pure planBoardSync planner the write path uses, the board updates that would mirror truth. Always report-only: renders the would-apply plan and writes nothing regardless of the enablement flag. Board/closure reads are fail-closed on gh auth (never degrade to falsely in-sync). npm control-plane:board-sync. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013 under VHS-REQ-691; ADR-0020.

Title: Governance Gate-Tooling Integrity
Notes: Dev-only sweep theme (epic #2159): declares the governance/CI gate tools (ADR index, agent-delegation, branch-protection, dev-dependency preflight, documentation workbench) as a manifest and fails closed when a declared gate script is missing on disk, its npm alias is absent, or the alias no longer invokes the declared script. Pure/injectable evaluateGovernanceGates; npm governance:gates. Converts these previously dev-only scripts into a requirement-mapped surface that cannot be silently deleted/renamed/unwired. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013; ADR-0021.

Title: Dev-Host And Build Tooling Integrity
Notes: Dev-only sweep theme (epic #2159): build-info contract integrity gate that runs the real generateBuildInfo read-only and fails closed when its emitted record does not satisfy the runtime consumer contract in src/tooling/buildInfo.ts (missing key, invalid/mismatched extensionVersion, malformed extensionCommit). Pure validateBuildInfoRecord; npm build-info:check. Maps the build/dev-host tooling (generator, consumer, dev-host loop/CLI) as a requirement surface. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013; ADR-0022.

Title: Public-Repo And CI Integration-Host Infrastructure
Notes: Dev-only sweep theme (epic #2159): maps the public-repo clone + CI integration-host infrastructure scripts as a requirement surface. Pure/injected parse/validate/command-plan boundaries unit-verifiable without a network, apt host, or display: Linux VS Code host bootstrap (os-release parse + apt install plan, public:host:bootstrap-linux), public-repo clone core + wrapper (supported-URL validation + remote-head-branch resolution + effective options, public:repo:clone), canonical icon-editor test-fixture wrapper (public:fixture:icon-editor), and the Linux (xvfb-run selection) + Windows (cmd.exe) integration-host launchers (test:integration:linux/windows). Adds first dedicated coverage for runWindowsIntegrationHost.buildWindowsIntegrationCommand. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013.

Title: Integration-Test Harness
Notes: Dev-only sweep theme (epic #2159): maps the VS Code extension-host integration-test harness as a requirement surface. Pure/unit-verifiable extension-payload staging (resolveIntegrationHostStageEntries parses package.json runtime deps + fixed roots; stageExtensionForWindowsHost copies into a fresh temp stage root, 100% unit-covered); real-VI workspace fixture (prepareIntegrationWorkspace uses genuine repository VIs, never synthetic stubs); integration runner selects host strategy + builds the extension-host control env (runTests.ts) and launches the suite (suite/index.ts) against the staged payload; compiled via its own tsconfig.integration.json to out-tests and run only through test:integration (never the unit-coverage gate). extensionHost.test.ts is the shared integration verification. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013; ADR-0024.

Title: Vagrant Maintainer Lane Helpers
Notes: Dev-only sweep theme (epic #2159): maps the optional local-only Vagrant maintainer-lane helpers as a requirement surface. Pure/injected parse/validate/arg boundaries unit-verifiable without a Vagrant or VirtualBox host: lane preflight/status (vagrant:preflight/vagrant:status), golden-box manifest verifier, release-lane + validation-proof guest helpers, box-provenance override + driver-arg parsers. Never a hosted-CI gate (VHS-REQ-599 forbids vagrant in workflows). Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013.

Title: Control-Plane Loop Drift Radar
Notes: Agent Operating Control-Plane loop (epic #2144): the read->shadow->apply loop. Radar: pure buildControlPlaneDigest composes board-vs-verified-truth drift (via the shadow board-sync planner) plus optional gate-health/open-work/debt sections into a marker-stamped sticky-issue digest; collector board read fails closed on gh auth; the workflow's own token is board-read-only (contents:read + issues:write). Tier-1 apply (slice 2): controlPlaneApply.js resolves only the two allowed targets (Status Done, Evidence Proven) through a closed field-map and applies verified closures via the governed write path (VHS-REQ-696), which is no-op unless control-plane-write.json enabled; the CI apply step is gated on the maintainer-provisioned CONTROL_PLANE_PROJECT_TOKEN secret (ambient token cannot edit Project #4). npm control-plane:digest / control-plane:apply. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013 under VHS-REQ-691; ADR-0023.

Title: Self-Hosted Integration-Coverage Lane
Notes: Dev-only sweep theme (epic #2159): a self-hosted lane that runs the coverage-excluded host-runner scripts to produce coverage evidence, plus a fail-closed security-contract gate. Pure evaluateIntegrationCoverageLane fails closed on any drift from the ratified posture (push/pull_request/schedule trigger, write token scope, unset permissions, non-self-hosted runner, missing trusted-ref guard). integration-coverage.yml is manual-dispatch-only, least-privilege contents:read, trusted-ref gated, advisory (gates no merges), Linux-first. The six host-runner scripts stay coverage-excluded; the lane exercises them for evidence. npm integration:coverage:check. Parent VHS-SYS-REQ-013; ADR-0024.

Title: Single-Pass Comparison Preview Pipeline
Notes: A comparison of two staged VI revisions is produced as a single pass modeled as a linear state machine over explicit typed states (STAGING, PREVIEW_LEFT, PREVIEW_RIGHT, VALIDATION, COMPARISON, UNSTAGING). runComparisonPreviewPipeline composes injected boundaries: idempotent stage/unstage, a per-side preview renderer, a comparison runner, a shared CycleMeter, and a StagedPreviewCache. VALIDATION admits the comparison only when both preview cycles loaded their staged VI; a rejection short-circuits (skips) the comparison (staged-vi-preview-validation-failed) and the pass reaches FAILED, else COMPLETE. UNSTAGING is idempotent, always-runs finally-style, owns cleanup of the staged inputs (removes the staged VI files + tree, skipping the legacy prune) and enumerates real stat-verified removedPaths/retainedPaths. Each result is tagged with its state and input. The shared CycleMeter measures each executed state (duration, monotonic index, inter-cycle latency). The StagedPreviewCache interface is defined for a later cache-loading slice and is not read in this pass. The integration seam maps the pass to retained per-state pipelineCycles evidence and classifies the preview-validation rejection; the staged-VI preview validator factory wires it always-on across providers into the live comparison runtime execution (a blocked/unavailable preview runtime passes the gate). A manual-dispatch hosted-CI workflow (windows-container-vi-compare.yml) exercises the pipeline against 64-bit LabVIEW on Windows via the windows-container provider on a pinned GitHub-hosted windows-2025 runner (not windows-latest, not self-hosted) and uploads schema-tagged evidence.
